questions.text: A browser requests a PHP page from a server. Which component normally processes its PHP instructions?
questions.explanation:
The interpreter runs PHP code on the web server before the response is sent.

Student note: PHP generates content on the server, not directly in the browser.

questions.text: Which option is a web browser rather than database or server software?
questions.explanation:
Chrome is a web browser used to request and view pages.

Student note: phpMyAdmin is a database administration tool, not a browser.

questions.text: In the address https://example.org/store, what is 'https' called?
questions.explanation:
The scheme tells the browser how to communicate with the destination.

Student note: HTTPS uses encryption to protect data in transit.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT itself a database server product?
questions.explanation:
Python is a programming language, while the other options name database systems.

Student note: A programming language can connect to a database without being a database server.

questions.text: Which application protocol is commonly used when a browser requests a webpage?
questions.explanation:
HTTP defines web requests and responses; secure websites usually use HTTPS.

Student note: Do not confuse HTTP web traffic with SMTP for sending email.

questions.text: With a standard XAMPP Apache setup, where do you normally place a new PHP website folder to serve it locally?
options: Inside the web browser installation folder
questions.explanation:
Apache's configured document root makes site files accessible over localhost.

Student note: A local web server can have a custom document root; htdocs is the usual XAMPP default.
